children: , the data-integration and artificial-intelligence platform company, won a Goldman Sachs upgrade as sovereign AI strengthened the growth case, with shares up about 2.4% at 11.20am EST to $203.57 Friday morning, Oct. 9. According to MarketWatch, the longtime skeptic moved to Buy from Neutral with a $230 target. That leaves roughly 13% upside from the latest price. Governments seeking greater control over their AI systems give investors another potential source of demand.

The growth numbers explain the enthusiasm. Palantir's second-quarter U.S. government revenue rose 90% to $809 million, while management lifted its full-year U.S. commercial revenue outlook above $3.424 billion, figures cited in Reuters' coverage of the market. Both businesses are expanding fast. But the valuation picture shows shares roughly 10% above the $185.07 GF Value estimate, leaving less room for execution slips.

The next test is profitability. National AI projects can bring larger contracts, but they can also demand more customization, tighter security and longer deployments. Palantir needs to reuse its software and deployment expertise across customers to keep those demands from swallowing the economics. Watch margins alongside revenue: expanding sales with disciplined delivery costs would give the sovereign AI thesis more financial weight.

title: Palantir Stocks Rise 2.4% as Goldman Backs Sovereign AI
